children: The S&P 500 (

) closed in the green on Friday, after the week saw the latest consumer inflation report coming in largely in line with expectations, as well as earnings reports from companies including Oracle and Adobe.
Nasdaq
and the Dow
fell roughly 1% for the week. Wall Street had a slew of upgrades and downgrades from analysts. Here are some of the major calls for the week:
Lockheed Martin upgraded on earnings growth expectations
UBS
Lockheed Martin
to Buy from Neutral, arguing that accelerating missile production, rising defense spending and growth beyond the company’s F-35 franchise could drive earnings above Wall Street expectations.
Analyst Gavin Parsons said he expects Lockheed’s

revenue to grow at a compound annual rate of approximately 9% through 2028, led by the missiles and fire control division. The bank forecasts companywide organic revenue growth of about 8% annually from 2025 through 2030.

The bank projects Lockheed revenue of $81.05 billion in 2026, $88.48 billion in 2027 and $96.13 billion in 2028. Its 2028 estimate is about 6% above consensus. UBS forecasts adjusted earnings of $30.69 a share in 2026, $34.50 in 2027 and $39.34 in 2028. The 2028 projection is 12% above the Wall Street consensus cited in the report.
JPMorgan upgrades Meta on AI potential
JPMorgan
Meta Platforms
to Overweight from Neutral, citing upside potential following the social media giant’s launch of its AI assistant.

“Meta is in the early stages of releasing frontier models and AI-driven products beyond advertising, notably Muse AI agent and Meta Model API access,” analyst Douglas Anmuth said, according to reports. PT was set to $820, implying a 25% increase from last close.
“Frontier models are at the core of Meta’s
product and monetization pipeline over a multi-year period, and its path toward superintelligence.”
Morgan Stanley cuts Novo Nordisk rating on semaglutide concern
Morgan Stanley downgraded Novo Nordisk
to Underweight from Equal-weight, saying that the overhang from the loss of exclusivity of semaglutide remains a key concern.

“The key issue of the investment case remains Novo's reliance on semaglutide (75% of sales in 2026e), which will face a large patent cliff in the early-mid 2030s across Europe and the US. We believe that the exposure to semaglutide will remain high at the start of the LOE impact from 2031 (we model 59% of sales in 2031),” the brokerage said.

Morgan Stanley analyst Thibault Boutherin forecasts Novo’s oral obesity franchise to reach $10 billion by 2031. However, the brokerage added that it is not expecting the obesity oral franchise to fully compensate for the headwinds faced by the company.
Northland Securities says Intel made 'material progress' in turnaround
Northland Securities upgraded Intel
to Outperform from Market Perform and said the company has made “material progress” in its turnaround.
Northland analyst Gus Richard noted Intel is likely to keep benefiting from the ongoing server CPU shortage. In addition, Intel's partnership with Tesla (
) on the Terafab semiconductor endeavor will “materially benefit” its foundry business. Richard put a $120 price target on Intel.
UBS cuts NuScale Power to Sell
UBS downgraded NuScale Power

to Sell from Neutral with a $6 price target, slashed from $10, saying the company's path to secure firm customer orders orders is increasingly difficult as peers make tangible commercial progress with competing designs.

UBS analyst Jon Windham expects only 2-4 advanced small modular reactor designs to scale to meet demand for commercial electricity generation, but with competitor projects already at or near construction and NuScale's estimated five-year lead time for plant construction and lack of firm customer commitments, he believes the company's path forward is increasingly difficult.
Deutsche Bank downgraded
Novartis
to Hold from Buy, citing recent failures in a pair of its late-stage trials that sent the stock sharply lower in the prior session. The analyst cut his price target on NVS to CHF120 from CHF140.
Dell Technologies
was in focus as Evercore upped its price target on the IT to $650 from $575 and kept it as a top pick, despite the recent surge in shares.
Morgan Stanley downgraded
Peloton Interactive

to an Underweight rating after having it lined up at Equal-weight. Analyst Nathan Feather and his team believe that negative earnings revisions will lead to more questions on the terminal value of the stock. Morgan Stanley lowered its price target on Peloton Interactive

title: Notable analyst calls this week: Lockheed Martin, Meta and Intel among top picks
